top_strength: The discovery was genuinely thorough and the pricing block was delivered nearly complete. She got all three addresses, floors at every stop, garage/shed items, parking at both ends, the gate-clearance problem, box count, and she actually asked the stressor question ('do you have any specific concern or stresser about the moving process in general?'). On pricing she opened with 'It's super simple', named the $210 rate, listed fuel/truck/taxes/insurance/wrap/pads/bands/tools, explained the $75 travel fee and why, delivered the no-hidden-fees list, and hit all three of No Worries, Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee in full. She also used the school bus equivalent for walk distance unprompted — 'we use the school bus as a reference for distance' — and the customer responded 'that's good cause I'm visual.'
coaching_note: Nicole, you lost a bookable move in the last ninety seconds of a call you had already done the hard work on. Highest-leverage fix: when the customer says 'that's a little bit more than my budget can afford,' that is the Save Your Ass cue, not the end of the call. She told you she was moving boxes herself and could take things in her car — you had a ready answer: 'Linda, the good news is you control a big piece of that number. Every box you get to the storage unit yourself, every drawer you empty, every carload you take shortens the clock — and since we only bill the time we use, that comes straight off the bill. A lot of customers cut an hour or more that way.' That reframes the quote instead of defending it. Second priority: you never asked for the business. You had her date, her three addresses, and her whole inventory, and you never said 'we do have September 18th open — no deposit required, so I can hold it for you right now and you can reply to the confirmation email with any corrections.' No deposit and the confirmation email are two of our strongest closers and neither appeared anywhere in this call. Third, use her name — once in fifteen minutes reads as transactional, and she ended the call without a goodbye from you. BUSINESS RISK: you quoted Mon-Thu at $202/hr as only '$8 less' than the Friday $210 two-mover rate. Please verify that spread against the current Garland rate card — if the real weekday rate is materially lower than $202, you talked a price-sensitive customer out of a booking on a wrong number. Second risk: this customer received a full verbal quote ($1,125-$1,335 plus a $75 travel fee) with no confirmation email and no follow-up commitment, and you told her to email the storage unit dimensions and unit number later without saying the estimate would be revised — so there is a verbal-only quote with unresolved inputs sitting outside EMMA.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and pleasant on the surface but heavily scripted — 'Okay, awesome' repeated verbatim throughout, constant 'Mm-hmm' filler, the customer's name used only once, and the clear budget cue drew no empathy or acknowledgment before the customer disengaged and ended the call herself.
